item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Necro-reply:
You missed something. The "transformation" is a hypnotic trick of the flashing color changes. So on video you only get a partial effect. The viewer can sort of see the monster, but it looks like a shadow on top of the real squid.

Technically, a still photo should look completely normal. Because in a pic you don't get any flashy-swirly lights to carry the hypnosis. But I liked the photoshop work someone donated, so I decided to let the technical inconsistency slide in favor of looking cool. :)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I view it as if this was actually a written document, so I really like the strikethroughs. It's as though it was written up and printed out, and this "snapshot" of the document is the printed and edited form in the filing cabinet, waiting to be picked up by a data entry clerk who will put the changes into the electronic database.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Easily one of my favorites. From the perspective of a marine biologist (who also happens to find cthulhu underwhelming) I found this incredibly entertaining. I am certain there are many anomalous entities that are much less dangerous in captivity than they appeared in the wild, and this speaks to the idea that with a little understanding, the world isn't as scary, isn't as deserving of hate, as the way people treat it…

While the addendum does reveal a mistake, I think it's absolutely within the Foundation's character to announce one of their agent's failings to kinda warn their other employees not to be incompetent a-holes.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very interesting concept, more so than just a scary creature. Reading through the crossed out text I kept thinking, "Why is this here? Wouldn't the Foundation delete this?" but then once I got to the reveal of what these things do and how it affected the Foundation personnel, I realized they really help to drive home the point.

At one point, the description of the creature that got crossed out, I read, "humanoid arms and legs ending in sharpened talons" and I really got the point this thing just hits you with a blast of nightmare fuel and scares the feces out of you. A common survival skill found in nature, amped up to 11.

+1

I love this one, on its own, but what takes it over the top to full-on greatness is something that's unintended and very likely in my head alone:

This SCP is only scary when you first see it, and eventually all the horror bleeds out. The SCP makes itself look like Cthulhu, part of a mythos that has been so overexposed and repeated that it, too, isn't very horrific anymore.
